key_insight: The paper establishes a temperature-corrected in-situ XRD workflow to more reliably identify phase transitions and decomposition in CsPbCl3 and extend the same thermal-analysis approach to Cs2AgSbCl6.
engineering_relevance: This improves the credibility of high-temperature stability testing for inorganic perovskites, which is critical for screening materials for durable solar cell absorber layers and related optoelectronic devices.
method: Ligand-assisted re-precipitation synthesis of CsPbCl3 as a model baseline.
In-situ temperature-dependent X-ray diffraction to track phase evolution and decomposition.
Control-substrate-based temperature calibration/refinement to estimate true sample temperature.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the method reproduced known high-temperature structural behavior in CsPbCl3 while enabling phase-transition and decomposition-temperature analysis for Cs2AgSbCl6.
watch_item: Results depend on accurate temperature calibration and the specific in-situ XRD setup, so apparent stability can be misleading if the true sample temperature is not well controlled.
paper_title: Thermal Corrections and Analysis on the Phase Stability of CsPbCl3 and Cs2AgSbCl6 during In-Situ Thermal Treatment
